children: Tata Steel Limited Sponsored GDR RegS (NSE:TATASTEEL) reported Q2 FY27 net profit of ₹3,700 crore, up 16.2%, revenue of ₹65,436 crore, up 11.5%, and EBITDA of ₹10,665 crore, up 17%. Auditors issued a modified opinion.
Previous Week Recap
Q2 Profit And Revenue Rise
: Tata Steel reported Q2 FY27 net profit up 16.2% to ₹3,700 crore, revenue up 11.5% to ₹65,436 crore and EBITDA up 17% to ₹10,665 crore. Shares fell 3.08% before rising 2%.
Results Approved; Modified Audit Opinion
: Tata Steel (TATASTEEL) said its board approved audited standalone and unaudited consolidated results for the quarter and half-year ended Sept. 30, 2026. Auditors issued a modified opinion.
Nomura Cuts Tata Steel Target

: Nomura kept its Buy rating on Tata Steel but cut its target to Rs 210 from Rs 240, citing weaker European earnings and possible captive iron ore mine losses by FY30. FY28–29 EBITDA forecasts fell 7%.
Targets Higher Iron Ore Sales
: Tata Steel (TATASTEEL) targets 10 million tonnes of domestic iron ore sales this fiscal year, up from about 2 million last year. It will supply its steel plants first, then sell surplus.
IG Metall Plans Wage Strike
: IG Metall plans a 24-hour strike affecting Tata Steel Limited Sponsored GDR RegS (TATASTEEL) amid a wage dispute. The union seeks higher pay and job protections; no strike date has been set.
Prabhudas Lilladher Raises Target

: Prabhudas Lilladher maintained its Accumulate rating on Tata Steel GDR and raised its target price to Rs 215, citing downstream capacity growth, a richer product mix and on-track upstream expansion.
Europe Operations Outlook Improves
: ICICI Securities expects Tata Steel’s Netherlands unit to benefit from stable operations and higher contract prices. UK losses may narrow as excess stock clears, with break-even targeted by Q4FY27.
Noel Naval Tata To Retire
: Tata Steel (TATASTEEL) said Vice Chairman Noel Naval Tata will retire as a non-executive director on November 11, 2026, after serving on the board since March 2022.
Amalgamation Awaits Tribunal Approval
: Tata Steel expects to complete the amalgamation of Neelachal Ispat Nigam this financial year, pending final National Company Law Tribunal approval, due for a hearing later this month.
Stake In Creative Port Rises
: Tata Steel converted 2.51 million preference shares in Creative Port Development into 38,222 equity shares, raising its stake from 51% to 57.5%. The company remains a subsidiary.
